resolvedFindings.issue: Plural availabilityNotes and sourceAvailability day restrictions disappeared from normalized public menu facts.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Plural notes, published days, date windows and weekdays are retained; explicit nonzero Oddle item/category status codes are excluded. Published ZZV restrictions and the newly published Oddle exclusions were checked.

resolvedFindings.issue: Greendot source names included outlet suffixes and had no aliases, preventing brand-only venue names from matching at the same address.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Compiler separates @ outlet suffixes into branch identity. Exact postal and existing unit checks remain in menu-match.ts. Brand-name success and wrong-postal rejection were checked.

resolvedFindings.issue: Timestamp sort could prune a newly saved ID and then write it outside retained metadata, exceeding the cache budget.
resolvedFindings.resolution: New entries are placed before sorted existing entries, so pruning retains them under timestamp ties and clock rollback. Actual service behavior passed byte and entry-count scenarios using future stored timestamps.

resolvedFindings.issue: Owned-menu fallback searched name and branch separately, so Greendot Bedok returned no result after branch identity was split from the name.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Search targets now combine each canonical/alias name with branch text while retaining postal-code search. Four actual-index brand/outlet/postal assertions pass.

resolvedFindings.issue: Opening the ledger before acquiring the pass lock could read a stale budget in a competing process; unflushed append completion did not establish durable reservation accounting.
resolvedFindings.resolution: The dedicated pass lock is acquired before ledger open/read. Every request/completion append uses flush:true. Mocked CLI ordering and actual ledger replay/cap probes pass.

resolvedFindings.issue: Writing an interim HTTP-error completion before retry backoff made an interrupted ID ineligible for ordinary resume.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Backoff leaves only its durable reservation. The next attempt gets a new reservation, stop checks prevent another fetch, and terminal transient failures have an explicit --retry-errors mode.

resolvedFindings.issue: Concurrency alone allowed request bursts that triggered rate-limit failures.
resolvedFindings.resolution: All workers and retries share 150-millisecond start spacing and a 60000-millisecond 429 cooldown with bounded stop-aware waits. Virtual-clock and final saved-outcome checks pass.

resolvedFindings.issue: A supplied single unit could mask a longer address-embedded unit range and yield an incorrect exact-unit proof in the first lookup batch.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Address-embedded ranges take precedence; range-versus-single fixtures reject the match. The stale hippo-real-food candidate was removed from the saved outcomes; all surviving candidates require review.

resolvedFindings.issue: The initial review stopped at ref-during-render and synchronous-effect state-update lint errors.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Summary ref synchronization now occurs in an effect; initial cache hydration is guarded before network work; the periodic load effect defers through a microtask. Final canonical lint and typecheck pass.

reviewedBehavior: Cache-before-network initialization, cold/deep-link summary arrival, route/fingerprint cleanup and acceptance guards were traced in useMenuDetail.
Index and detail refresh intervals, offline retention, error/Retry paths, response byte limits and quota rejection were inspected.
Correction lookup uses separately loaded branch details; draft proposals preserve their branch and do not mutate published menus.
Publication is gated by explicit manifest entries, source fingerprints and generated-output consistency checks; held research is not automatically published.
Standalone prices are not promoted from listingPrice; price options, fees, unknown currency and source-specific qualifiers remain explicit.
MenuDishes mounts at most 40 matching rows per page, with separate source/category selection and on-demand option expansion.
Shared section.itemNotice removes only an identical literal qualifier prefix from every source item and renders that notice before the dishes.
Identity requests use the fixed Places host and literal field mask; API keys stay in request headers and are not persisted in receipts or public data.
Durable request reservation occurs before gate admission; stop is checked before reservation and after admission. All retries share the same cap and gate.
Identity candidate display facts are copied from independently sourced leads, and the runner does not modify publication manifests or public menus.
Explore alone opts into suggestionsInFlow, leaving the autocomplete panel in normal layout above owned-menu results while preserving the shared picker's default dropdown behavior.
The location lookup spinner explicitly exposes the accessible name Finding locations.

The menu withdrawal API reads one complete local-store revision without a writer lease; writers flush a temporary complete revision then atomically replace records.json, and malformed reviews fail closed.
The offline identity analysis script was read and linted; its existing output was inspected without rerunning its file-writing entry point.
historicalGateNote: The first broad eslint command reported unrelated avatar-security.cjs errors outside this review scope. Final canonical Expo lint and separately scoped publication-script lint pass; this is not a claim that every unrelated CJS script passes broad lint.
limitations: This approves the specified source and generated-menu scope after the recorded fixes; it does not establish that all researched restaurants or the candidate directory have complete menus.

No paid Google or other outbound provider calls were made by this reviewer. Field-tier documentation was checked on Google's official documentation; synthetic and memory-adapter probes made zero real network requests.

Storage scenarios used the actual service with a memory adapter. Device AsyncStorage capacity, native browser/network transitions and physical-device rendering/performance require their separate acceptance evidence.
Hook transitions were reviewed statically; publication/schema/cache assertions do not constitute live browser or native end-to-end verification.

The public catalogue probe invoked server functions directly. Live browser/native appearance, request transport and deployment acceptance require their separate evidence; the runtime must load the regenerated static publication.
The 2500 cap is durable conservative reservation accounting, including retries and reservations retained after interruption; it is not an assertion of an exact billed amount.
